text: New to investing?
Here are five ETFs to know and what you're actually buying with each one.
Think of an ETF like a basket.
You buy one fund, and that fund holds a bunch of stocks.
Here's what's inside each one.
First, VOO.
This is one I own.
It holds about five hundred big US companies.
So you get a piece of companies like Apple and Microsoft in one purchase.
Then there's VTI.
You still get Apple and Microsoft, plus a bunch of smaller companies.
It covers almost the entire US stock market.
VT takes it worldwide.
It has US companies and companies from other countries all in one fund.
VXUS is the overseas part.
If you already own VOO and want to add companies outside the US, that's what VXUS can do.
And SCHD focuses on US companies that pay dividends.
A dividend is a cash payment you can receive for owning shares.
The amount can change.
So do you need all five?
VOO, VTI, and VT already hold a lot of the same big US companies.
If I wanted one fund for US and international stocks, I'd look at VT first.
This is for education only and isn't financial advice.
Save this for when you're comparing your first ETF.
